title: Loom Pricing 2026: Free and Paid Plans Explained
summary: Loom pricing includes a free plan plus two paid tiers charged per creator, meaning your costs grow as you add team members.
body_markdown:
## Automating the Loom usage check with Activepieces


Nothing here replaces Loom.


Activepieces runs the rule from the last section on a schedule, at 1 credit a run however many steps it has, so someone is asked to compare creator count and recording volume against the plan's limits before a recording fails instead of after.


Titled "HubSpot Tickets Categorization", the flow below isn't a Loom workflow. It is a ticket-routing flow, and it shows what the builder gives you: a trigger at the top, AI steps, a Router that branches, and Slack "Send Message" steps at the bottom.


With the trigger selected, the panel on the right asks for a Connection and offers "Load Sample Data". Take from it the shape, not the content. Swap the trigger for a schedule and the Slack steps stay exactly as they are.


You don't have to draw that flow by hand: describe the monthly check in the built-in chat and it publishes a live flow in your account, under the same RBAC and audit logs as one someone built manually.


The first scheduled Monday produces a run trace listing the outcome of every step, including which branch the Router took.


The 746 integrations are the folders in the open source monorepo's community directory on GitHub, so whether a Loom integration exists is a folder name you can look up before relying on one.


What follows is how that shape applies to a usage check.


### What the scheduled Loom usage check does


On the first working day of each month, say, the trigger fires on a calendar. A first step asks the plan owner to enter two things: how many people currently hold a creator seat, and roughly how many recordings the team made.


Next, a Router compares those entries with the limits you copied from Loom's pricing page. One branch means the team's inside its limits and sends a short note.


The other branch means it's at or past a limit, and it posts to Slack or email naming which one.


You type in every limit in that comparison. If Loom changes a cap, the workflow keeps comparing against the old one until someone edits it. For a team of three, this is overbuilt. A recurring calendar reminder does the same job with less to maintain.


### What it cannot see in Loom


Check first whether any of the 746 integrations is a Loom one that reads seat and recording data, so you can't identify it at a glance. Don't assume it does.


Until you have confirmed it in the integration list, treat the workflow as blind to Loom: it knows only what a person tells it.


If another admin added a creator last week, that creator doesn't appear unless someone counts again.


The check prompts a human to look; it doesn't look for them. It also can't tell you how Loom defines a creator in edge cases, so that definition still has to come from Loom's own pages.
